findings.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.java:57 — Default, Elytron, and FIPS providers share priority 200, so ambiguous configurations silently resolve by service discovery order and may select non-FIPS cryptography. Reject providers tied at the highest priority.
ASN1Decoder.java:59 — readSequence() accepts children exceeding the declared sequence boundary because a negative remaining length terminates the loop instead of triggering rejection.

ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:43 — All three tests use the same unspecified default EC curve, so ES384 and ES512 lack guaranteed P-384 and P-521 coverage, including P-521 long-form DER sequence lengths. Initialize the key generator with each algorithm’s corresponding curve.

goldens.comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)

Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: CryptoIntegration.java:57 — Default, Elytron, and FIPS providers share priority 200, so ambiguous configurations silently resolve by service discovery order and may select non-FIPS cryptography. Reject providers tied at the highest priority.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The golden comment identifies a bug where the wrong provider is returned (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle). The candidate issue discusses ambiguous priority configurations (multiple providers sharing priority 200) that could result in selecting the wrong provider (non-FIPS cryptography). Both issues are about the same underlying problem: incorrect provider selection due to priority/ordering issues. The candidate identifies the root cause (tied priorities) that leads to the symptom described in the golden comment (wrong provider returned).

per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify the same underlying issue: when length is -1 (from indefinite-length encoding), the arithmetic involving length behaves unexpectedly. The golden comment points out that 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly with -1. The candidate comment identifies that 'a negative remaining length terminates the loop instead of triggering rejection' - this is describing the same problem where the negative length value causes incorrect processing behavior. Both are pointing to the bug where indefinite-length encoding (length = -1) leads to incorrect handling in the sequence reading logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:43 — All three tests use the same unspecified default EC curve, so ES384 and ES512 lack guaranteed P-384 and P-521 coverage, including P-521 long-form DER sequence lengths. Initialize the key generator with each algorithm’s corresponding curve.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that ECDSAAlgorithmTest uses KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() without specifying a curve, meaning all three tests (ES256, ES384, ES512) use the same default curve (likely P-256). This means the tests don't actually verify the ASN1 encoding/decoding works correctly for P-384 and P-521 curves, which have different key sizes and could produce different DER encoding lengths. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added crypto code, though not a bug in the production code itself.
